Failure modes include degraded transfer to electrode montages or recording conditions outside the pretraining distribution and the general risk that an unreviewed arXiv preprint's cross-device claims do not hold on the reader's hardware or subjects. 1 independent implementation, 4 stars. Research area: other. Recommendation: not applicable.

item.title: Memory-Centric Continual Learning for AI Agents
item.description: The framework proposes replacing passive retrieval-cache memory with a continual-learning view of agent memory, organized by substrates, assets, and policies with an inner state-update loop and an outer policy-refinement loop. It is a taxonomy plus evaluation and scaling methodology, so adoption costs engineering effort to redesign memory systems and evaluation pipelines, but it provides no concrete algorithm or implementation to deploy directly. It can fail to yield behavioral gains if memory writes are noisy or policies are not tuned, since the abstract reports no empirical results demonstrating that the approach improves future actions. 3 independent implementations, 132 stars. Research area: memory and context. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: Right On Q: Recovering Reasoning under Quantization via Self-Generated Trajectories
item.description: OnQ replaces fixed-response teacher supervision in quantization-aware training with on-policy distillation, where the full-precision teacher supervises the quantized student on the student's own generated prefixes, weighted candidate-wise by Dynamic KL. It costs a full training pipeline rather than post-training calibration: student rollout generation plus teacher forward passes per step, which raises compute and implementation complexity beyond block-wise calibration alone. It can fail when the teacher itself is unreliable on student-generated prefixes, when budget limits prevent multiple QAT runs, and its results are demonstrated only on Qwen3 models up to 8B, so transfer to other families or larger scales is unverified. 2 independent implementations, 126 stars. Research area: quantization. Recommendation: test.

item.title: A KAN-based Non-linear Factorization for Embedding Layer Compression
item.description: It replaces the purely linear low-rank decomposition of an embedding matrix with a factorization that inserts learnable univariate (KAN-style) nonlinear projections inside the compressed embedding layer, optionally initialized from a pretrained uncompressed embedding and refined with distillation. The cost is additional per-parameter compute for the learnable univariate functions, extra implementation complexity over a standard two-matrix factorization, and a refinement/distillation phase to recover quality. It can fail because evidence is limited to Skip-gram word2vec-style embeddings on analogy and similarity benchmarks, so gains may not transfer to large transformer embedding tables, and KAN function evaluation may erode the latency and memory savings the compression was meant to provide. 1 independent implementation, 122 stars. Research area: efficient architectures. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Harness Scaling for Generalizable Agentic Reinforcement Learning
item.description: Harness Scaling replaces agentic RL performed through a single fixed harness with RL conducted across a factorized, systematically sampled set of harness configurations, which the authors report improves generalization to unseen white-box and black-box harnesses. Its cost is substantial: it requires RL training runs across multiple harness configurations, repeated for several model scales and algorithms, which demands training compute, harness engineering, and evaluation infrastructure well beyond a single 24 GB GPU or API-only setup. Adoption can fail if the factorized harness space omits the dimensions that matter for a deployment harness, if the balanced factorial subset is too small to induce transfer, or if the reader's underlying API model cannot be fine-tuned at all, in which case the method is inapplicable. 4 independent implementations, 15 stars. Research area: tool use. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: RCSD: Reinforcement and Continual Learning for Domain-Specific Speculative Decoding
item.description: RCSD replaces soft-label distillation of the draft model with a reinforcement-style objective trained on accepted/rejected token pairs collected during speculative inference, optimizing acceptance length directly rather than distribution mimicry. The cost is a custom training pipeline: speculative decoding must already run in production to harvest preference pairs, plus masked-loss training infrastructure and continual updates as traffic shifts, though the resulting draft model remains small and inference-time memory is unchanged. It can fail if production traffic drifts from the training distribution (acceptance rates decay, requiring retraining cycles), if the small team cannot maintain the data-collection loop, or on workloads where speculative decoding itself offers little headroom (e.g., low-batch or highly deterministic generation). 1 independent implementation, 122 stars. Research area: speculative decoding. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Stochastic Pruning of the DPO Computation Graph: 1.4x Faster Training and Lower Peak Memory
item.description: The method replaces the standard concatenated DPO training step with stochastic sampling of scored response positions, executed prefixes, and backpropagated preference branches, omitting the corresponding computation before it occurs. It costs a modified training objective (partially corrected with inverse-probability weighting for single-branch gradients), added implementation complexity in the training loop, and slightly lower mean accuracy with benchmark-dependent changes in open-ended generation scores. It can fail if the accuracy degradation is unacceptable for the target task, if the claimed savings do not transfer beyond the two model families evaluated, or if the unbiased estimator's higher variance destabilizes convergence on the reader's data distribution. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: efficient training. Recommendation: test.

item.title: RISK-KV: Quality-Aware Selective KV Cache Reconstruction for Distributed LLM Inference
item.description: RISK-KV replaces full KV cache retention/transfer and full token replay during request migration and interruption recovery, reconstructing missing layers' KV states via cross-layer ridge regression folded into the model's projection matrices. It costs a topology search with quality gating, per-layer-group predictor fitting, storage for regression parameters, and a measured NLL degradation that must stay under the gating threshold. It can fail if reconstruction error exceeds the quality gate on out-of-distribution inputs, if the 512-token-history speedup does not generalize to longer contexts, or if the reader's workload lacks migration/recovery events frequent enough to amortize the search and fitting overhead. 1 independent implementation, 4 stars. Research area: KV cache. Recommendation: test.

item.title: PACE: Periodic and Channel-Aligned Encoding of Four-Bit Recurrent States
item.description: PACE replaces per-token rounding of the recurrent state in linear-attention and hybrid models (e.g., 8-bit DAMP or Q-Mamba) with post-hoc 4-bit quantization that rounds only once every few tokens, shares scales per column, and keeps error-sensitive heads at 8 bits. It requires a small token buffer between rounding points and mixed-precision head handling, adding modest kernel and serving complexity; accuracy on the 4B model is not fully preserved at 4 bits. Failure modes include quality degradation on smaller models, dependence on chunked-kernel serving stacks that support buffered decoding, and sensitivity to workloads dominated by long concurrent generations where state memory is not the actual bottleneck. 1 independent implementation, 122 stars. Research area: quantization. Recommendation: test.

item.title: TernScope: Model-Hardware Co-Design for Efficient Ternary Endoscopic Segmentation
item.description: TernScope replaces full-precision or 8-bit convolutional segmentation with a co-designed ternary-weight (W2/A8) network trained via progressive quantization-aware training from deep to shallow layers. The claimed gains (multiplier-free compute, packed storage, 88.46% area reduction) materialize only on custom systolic-array silicon; on a 24 GB GPU, ternary weights provide no practical speed or memory benefit without specialized kernels, and the model is already small enough that deployment constraints are unlikely to bind. Failure modes include accuracy loss on out-of-domain endoscopy data from aggressive quantization, engineering cost of the TPQ pipeline, and the fact that none of the hardware advantages transfer to commodity GPU inference. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: quantization. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: Effects of Model Scale and Quantization on Social Bias and Abstention in Question Answering
item.description: It replaces single-metric fairness checks (counting biased responses on BBQ) with a joint evaluation that tracks bias, abstention rate, prompt formulation, and answer-option design together when selecting model size and quantization settings. It costs only additional evaluation passes on existing benchmarks and forces disclosure of over-abstention, adding modest evaluation compute and reporting complexity. It can fail if BBQ results are treated as representative of production distributions, since the paper shows trends are not stable across prompt formulations, model families, or forced-choice settings, so conclusions may not transfer. 1 independent implementation, 122 stars. Research area: safety and guardrails. Recommendation: adopt.

item.title: SPARE: Sparsity Allocation via Routing Entropy for Efficient MoEs
item.description: SPARE replaces uniform per-layer expert pruning budgets with a layer-wise allocation derived from routing entropy measured on calibration data, applied on top of any existing expert selector. It is training-free, so its cost is a calibration forward pass and the engineering of pruning and remapping experts; the pruned model is smaller in memory but loses capacity relative to the dense model. It can fail when calibration data is unrepresentative of production traffic, since routing entropy estimates then misallocate the pruning budget, and gains shrink at low pruning ratios where uniform allocation is already adequate. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: sparsity and pruning. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Uni-Mem: Learning a Long-Horizon Agentic Memory Manager with Unified Online Policy Optimization
item.description: Replaces hand-designed memory workflows and hybrid RL-plus-offline-supervision pipelines with a single policy trained end-to-end online for both memory construction and retrieval, using stage-decoupled group comparisons and event-level credit assignment. Costs include an online RL training loop over long memory trajectories, the added complexity of alternating stage optimization, and dependence on RL-quality reward signals; the abstract gives no compute or latency figures. Can fail if rewards are sparse or misaligned, if benchmarks like LoCoMo do not transfer to the reader's workloads, or if the trained policy is brittle under distribution shift in production interactions. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: memory and context. Recommendation: watch.
